newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dutch central banker confirmed in EU post.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central banker confirmed in EU post.

text.p: Dutch central bank chief Wim Duisenberg, widely regarded as the architect of the Netherlands' strong economy, was confirmed on Friday as the next president of the EU's European Monetary Institute (EMI) from July 1, 1997.
The EMI is the forerunner of the European Central Bank which will govern the European Union's monetary policy from January 1, 1999 under its planned economic and monetary union (EMU).
European Union leaders attending the Dublin summit formally approved Duisenberg to succeed Belgium's Alexandre Lamfalussy who will stay on as EMI chief until next summer.
Duisenberg, 60, currently Europe's longest-serving central bank chief, is firm favourite to head the new central bank and oversee the introduction of a single currency.

Under his stewardship, the Netherlands has emerged from years of welfare over-spending to become a shining example of monetary stability, with its strong guilder, low inflation and unemployment and tight fiscal policy.
As such, it is widely regarded as a model for Europe's economic future.
